behavioral_notes.observation: mail.group does NOT inherit mail.thread; it inherits only mail.alias.mixin. message_post is custom-overridden (models/mail_group.py:280): it builds a mail.message via mail.thread._message_create, then wraps it in a mail.group.message, sets moderation_status ('pending_moderation' if group.moderation else 'accepted'), links the group-message parent for threading, and either calls _notify_members (open group) or queues for moderation. message_new/message_update are no-op stubs so the inbound mail gateway routes to this custom flow.

Accepted messages fan out to every member email by creating mail.mail rows (NOT via the follower/notification pipeline). Each mail carries RFC-2369 list headers (List-Id, List-Archive, List-Post, List-Subscribe) and an RFC-8058 one-click List-Unsubscribe header, plus a per-member QWeb footer with mailto/group/unsubscribe links; the author is skipped and sends are batched (GROUP_SEND_BATCH_SIZE=500 / mail.session.batch.size).

action_moderate_accept/reject/allow/ban gate each pending mail.group.message (models/mail_group_message.py); accept triggers _notify_members, reject can email the author a comment via mail.group.message.reject. allow/ban create a persistent mail.group.moderation white/black-list rule (email+status, unique per group) and cascade the decision to all same-author pending messages. _cron_notify_moderators pushes Inbox/Email reminders (mail.thread.message_notify) to moderators with messages awaiting action.

_alias_get_error enforces access_mode at the alias: 'groups' mode rejects senders not in access_group_id, 'members' mode rejects non-members (returns AliasError). _routing_check_route bounces inbound email to a closed group (renders email_template_mail_group_closed via _routing_create_bounce_email). Posting through the alias therefore creates a group thread or a moderated/rejected message depending on sender identity and group state.

Public-user subscribe/unsubscribe is double-opt-in: /group/subscribe sends a confirmation email carrying an hmac action token, and /group/subscribe-confirm (/unsubscribe-confirm) validates it before _join_group/_leave_group. Logged users join/leave immediately. /group/<id>/unsubscribe_oneclick is POST-only, csrf-disabled, consteq-validated against a per-email hmac token to honour mail-client one-click unsubscribe. Joining a moderated group with moderation_guidelines auto-emails the guidelines template.

2 JS files registered as website public.interactions (mail_group.mail_group, mail_group.mail_group_message) under web.assets_frontend; no OWL components, no registry field/view widgets, no patches. Portal archive/thread pages are server-rendered QWeb (controllers/portal.py + views/portal_templates.xml); backend adds only a stylesheet (web.assets_backend).

information_flows: side-effect: inbound email -> mail.alias -> mail.group.message_post -> mail.message + mail.group.message
side-effect: mail.group._notify_members -> mail.mail (fan-out to members, List-* headers)

capabilities: Subscription Management (join/leave, double opt-in, one-click unsubscribe)
value_streams: Post-to-distribute: member email -> alias gateway -> (moderation) -> fan-out to all members + portal archive
policies: 10 record rules: portal/public visibility scoping of groups & messages
access_mode (public / members / groups) gates who may read and email the list
moderation flag + mail.group.moderation white/black list gate message publication
is_closed bounces inbound email and blocks joining

classification.rationale: mail_group is a value-network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology): the list is the intermediary that connects a community of subscribers to one another, and value rises with membership (network effect) rather than flowing along a transformation chain. Its core service is mediation/relationship-brokering - registering members (mail.group.member), routing each posted message to every other member (_notify_members fan-out), and maintaining the shared archive - not converting an input into an output (chain) or matching a problem to expertise (shop). Moderation (mail.group.moderation) is the network 'admission/contract management' control. Classed primary because operating the discussion-group community is the module's own end-product; mapped to APQC 9.4 (internal communications) as the closest PCF process for running a list/community communications channel.

standard_capabilities: email-driven mailing lists with auto-created alias (mail.alias.mixin)
self-service subscribe/unsubscribe (portal, confirmation email, RFC 8058 one-click)
three privacy modes (public / members-only / selected user group)
message moderation with per-author allow/ban lists and reject-with-comment
public threaded web archive with monthly archive navigation
moderator reminder cron + new-member guidelines email
typical_fits: internal/community discussion groups reachable by email and web
standards-compliant list headers (List-Id / List-Unsubscribe) for deliverability
common_gaps: no bounce-driven auto-unsubscribe or per-member delivery health
moderation rules are exact-email allow/ban only (no regex / content filters)
no double-opt-in audit / GDPR consent log beyond the hmac token flow
